title: orient refreshes decay timers for lessons it never emits
description:
Found by codex adversarial review of sutra/277-279.

sutra/277 made orient call query_for_context_capped(ctx, usize::MAX) per component file so the merged `lessons_omitted` count would be honest. But that helper records `last_surfaced` for everything it returns, so orient marked the entire candidate set across every file in the component — including the lessons its own ORIENT_LESSON_CAP then dropped.

archive_decayed (src/lessons.rs) spares any unverified lesson whose last_surfaced is within the 90-day window. So a broad directory-anchored lesson — matching every file in the component, and the least useful thing in the response — was kept permanently unarchivable without ever being shown to anyone. The decay lifecycle became a function of internal candidate matching rather than actual surfacing.

acceptance_criteria.text: Only lessons actually serialized into the orient response refresh last_surfaced
Lessons dropped by ORIENT_LESSON_CAP keep last_surfaced NULL and stay archiveable
Regression test verified to fail under the previous behaviour

execution_record:
Fix splits the two concerns with a Surfacing::{Record,Deferred} flag plus a public mark_surfaced(ids); orient defers, caps the merged set, then marks exactly what it serialized. Added LessonsDb::last_surfaced as an observable for the regression test, which was verified to fail under the old Record semantics before being accepted.

NOTE: the commit message says "(sutra/280)" — wrong task number, sutra/280 was already used by 91fedc7. The correct reference is sutra/285. Not amended because that rewrites history; flagged to Josh instead.

Also in the same commit: a search test exercising query+category+symbol+verified+project simultaneously, closing the bind-index coverage gap from sutra/279 (each tier allocates its own bind slots, and `verified` adds a condition with no bind, so an off-by-one binds the wrong value silently rather than erroring). Writing it surfaced a test-fixture trap: citations are idempotent per task_id, so citing twice with task_id=None leaves confidence at 1 and never verifies.
root_cause: query_for_context_capped conflated retrieval with surfacing bookkeeping: it recorded last_surfaced for every lesson it returned, which is correct only when the caller shows everything it receives. sutra/277 introduced a caller that deliberately over-fetches (usize::MAX) in order to compute an honest merged omitted count, and that broke the helper's implicit assumption — the write happened at the wrong layer, one cap too early.
